raw.query: WITH poly AS (SELECT p99_ttft_ms, max_ttft_ms, (metrics->>'max_itl_ms')::double precision AS max_itl_ms FROM provenance.llm_run_summary WHERE run_id = 'srcbuild:llm_head2k_poly_src'), aic AS (SELECT p99_ttft_ms, max_ttft_ms, (metrics->>'max_itl_ms')::double precision AS max_itl_ms FROM provenance.llm_run_summary WHERE run_id = 'srcbuild:llm_head2k_aic_src') SELECT (aic.p99_ttft_ms / poly.p99_ttft_ms) AS ttft_p99_ratio, (aic.max_ttft_ms / poly.max_ttft_ms) AS ttft_max_ratio, (aic.max_itl_ms / poly.max_itl_ms) AS itl_max_ratio FROM poly, aic;
raw.observed: TTFT p99 ratio = 1.24x (307.36ms vs 248.46ms), TTFT max ratio = 1.78x (4517.57ms vs 2539.91ms), ITL max ratio = 1.92x (347.73ms vs 180.70ms)
raw.claimed: TTFT p99 grows 1.24x, maximum TTFT grows 1.8x, and inter-token latency roughly doubles (1.9x)
raw.evidence: The claim is fully supported by comparing calibrated timing (aic) and polynomial timing (poly) in llm_run_summary. Metrics align exactly: TTFT p99 grows 1.24x (307.36/248.46 = 1.237), TTFT max grows 1.78x ≈ 1.8x (4517.57/2539.91 = 1.779), and max ITL grows 1.92x ≈ 1.9x (347.73/180.70 = 1.924). Prior verifiers mistakenly evaluated mean_itl (1.13x) or p99_itl (0.76x) instead of max_itl (ITL max).
